### Using derived subcommands in a builder application

When using the derive API, you can use `#[command(subcommand)]` inside the struct to add
subcommands. The type of the field is usually an enum that derived `Parser`. However, you can
also add the subcommands in that enum to a `Command` instance created with the builder API.

It uses the [`Subcommand::augment_subcommands`][crate::Subcommand::augment_subcommands] method
to add the subcommands to the `Command` instance.

### Adding hand-implemented subcommands to a derived application

When using the derive API, you can use `#[command(subcommand)]` inside the struct to add
subcommands. The type of the field is usually an enum that derived `Parser`. However, you can
also implement the `Subcommand` trait manually on this enum (or any other type) and it can
still be used inside the struct created with the derive API. The implementation of the
`Subcommand` trait will use the builder API to add the subcommands to the `Command` instance
created behind the scenes for you by the derive API.

Notice how in the previous example we used
[`augment_subcommands`][crate::Subcommand::augment_subcommands] on an enum that derived
`Parser`, whereas now we implement
[`augment_subcommands`][crate::Subcommand::augment_subcommands] ourselves, but the derive API
calls it automatically since we used the `#[command(subcommand)]` attribute.

### Flattening hand-implemented args into a derived application

When using the derive API, you can use `#[command(flatten)]` inside the struct to add arguments as
if they were added directly to the containing struct. The type of the field is usually an
struct that derived `Args`. However, you can also implement the `Args` trait manually on this
struct (or any other type) and it can still be used inside the struct created with the derive
API. The implementation of the `Args` trait will use the builder API to add the arguments to
the `Command` instance created behind the scenes for you by the derive API.

Notice how in the previous example we used [`augment_args`][crate::Args::augment_args] on the
struct that derived `Parser`, whereas now we implement
[`augment_args`][crate::Args::augment_args] ourselves, but the derive API calls it
automatically since we used the `#[command(flatten)]` attribute.

analysis.summary: Analyzed only the supplied clap 4.6.7 evidence. Eight complete src/main.rs recipes cover derive, builder, help, deferred subcommands, metadata macros, interoperation, escapes, and optional values. All 122 inventory entries are accounted for. Empty include fragments and historical syntax are distinguished from usable examples. Recipes have not been compiled or tested; evidence coverage is sampled.

findings.title: Follow the release manifest and enforced std requirement
findings.guidance: Use Rust 1.85 or newer for clap 4.6.7. Keep std enabled, including when disabling default features: the implementation rejects builds without it. The overview's MSRV 1.74 and feature reference's description of std as unused are stale relative to the manifest and compile-time guard.

findings.title: Choose the API and enable only the needed optional features
findings.guidance: Prefer derive for a fixed CLI whose values should become Rust fields. Choose builder when inspecting argument order or value sources, or when constructing the interface at runtime. Enable derive explicitly; cargo, env, string, and wrap_help are separate opt-ins for their respective capabilities.

findings.title: Match argument actions, field types, and getters
findings.guidance: In builder code, use SetTrue for switches, Count for repeated flags, Set for a single value, and Append for repeated values. Read these with get_flag, get_count, get_one, and get_many respectively. Derive infers bool as a switch, Option<T> as optional, T as required unless defaulted, and Vec<T> as repeated.

findings.title: Separate effective values from explicit occurrences
findings.guidance: Do not use contains_id to decide whether a boolean switch was supplied: the supplied tests show that its default false value also creates an entry. Use get_flag for the effective boolean and value_source when provenance matters. Repeated Set or SetTrue arguments conflict by default; choose Append, Count, or args_override_self(true) deliberately.

findings.title: Set named-option requiredness explicitly
findings.guidance: arg!(--config <FILE>) requires a value when the option appears, but does not require the option itself. Add .required(true) when config must be supplied. The macro example's help text calls the file required without setting this requirement; do not copy that implication.

findings.title: Check both configuration and parsing behavior
findings.guidance: Add a test calling Command::debug_assert, using CommandFactory::command for a derived parser. Use explicit argument iterators and fallible parsing to check valid inputs and rejected inputs without exiting the test process. Configuration checks complement behavioral assertions.

findings.title: Control short and long help deliberately
findings.guidance: Use doc comments for help summaries and a blank line followed by details for long help. -h selects short text and --help selects long text. Explicit attributes override inferred documentation; clear an unwanted long description with #[command(long_about = None)].

findings.title: Do not infer flags from help comments
findings.guidance: The two Foo help examples are not equivalent CLI declarations: the first has #[arg(short)] and the second does not. Doc comments supply help text, not flag spelling. Add short or long explicitly when adapting a documented field into an option.

findings.title: Opt into deferred subcommand construction
findings.guidance: In 4.6.7, opt into lazy subcommand argument construction with #[command(defer = true)] on a Parser or Subcommand enum. It defaults to false without unstable-v5. Put parent-help metadata on enum variants, configure nested enums separately, and call Command::build before inspecting deferred arguments. Parsing builds selected commands automatically.

findings.title: Reuse derived types inside builder applications
findings.guidance: Combine builder and derive with Args::augment_args or Subcommand::augment_subcommands, then convert the resulting matches through FromArgMatches. This lets reusable derived argument sets participate in a builder-owned interface.

findings.title: Read application package metadata with the cargo feature
findings.guidance: Enable cargo for command! and crate_* metadata macros. They read the consuming package's Cargo metadata at compile time. crate_name! uses CARGO_PKG_NAME; use the appropriate Cargo environment variable directly if the binary or crate name differs.

findings.title: Preserve argument boundaries and explicit escapes
findings.guidance: Pass already separated arguments to clap; parsing a shell command string requires a separate tokenizer. Use last(true) for a positional accessible only after --. Use allow_hyphen_values or allow_negative_numbers only when the argument's grammar calls for them.

findings.title: Model absent, bare, and explicit option values
findings.guidance: For a color-style option, combine num_args(0..=1), require_equals, a default value, and default_missing_value to distinguish omission, a bare --color, and --color=never. ValueEnum constrains the accepted values and permits default_value_t without a Display implementation.

recipes.title: Build a typed CLI with defaults and configuration checks
recipes.description: Parse a required name and a typed default count from explicit inputs, with a configuration test. In an application entry point, Cli::parse() reads process arguments and handles CLI exits.

recipes.title: Convert builder matches into application data
recipes.description: Declare matching builder arguments before converting ArgMatches into an application struct. The documentation's derive cfg guards are unnecessary here because no clap derive macro is used.

recipes.title: Generate help from comments and explicit overrides
recipes.description: Render short and long help, override inferred text with attributes, and explicitly retain option spelling when using doc comments.

recipes.title: Compose typed subcommands with deferred construction
recipes.description: Compose reusable Args, a required subcommand, and an enum-valued option. Opt into the new 4.6.7 defer attribute and build before inspecting deferred arguments.

recipes.title: Use Cargo metadata and concise argument macros
recipes.description: Combine Cargo metadata macros with arg! declarations. The no_run metadata snippets are adapted to explicit inputs, and config requiredness is set explicitly.

recipes.title: Mix builder configuration with derived argument types
recipes.description: Attach derived arguments and subcommands to a builder command and recover their typed values through FromArgMatches.

recipes.title: Capture positional values after --
recipes.description: Capture an escaped positional tail while preserving a hyphen-prefixed value and an already-tokenized value containing spaces.

recipes.title: Accept an option with an optional enum value
recipes.description: Distinguish an omitted option, a bare switch-like option, and an explicit enum value. Explicit values must use the equals form.
